result.paraphrase:
Image-based indoor localization has attracted considerable recent interest because it needs no infrastructure support. However, prior image-based localization methods often rely on servers to handle queries because of their storage and computation demands. This does not scale well, adds round-trip delay, and requires continuous network connectivity. Many methods also ask users to manually verify the shortlisted matching landmarks, which is inconvenient, slow, and error-prone.

To address these issues, we propose HAIL, a highly automated image-based localization algorithm for mobile devices, with automation focused on image confirmation after taking images. HAIL improves storage and processing efficiency by retaining only distinctive visual features for each landmark and using an efficient k-d tree for feature search. It also leverages motion sensors and map constraints to improve localization accuracy without user intervention. We implemented HAIL on Android platforms and carried out extensive experiments in a food plaza and a premium shopping mall. The results show that it achieves much higher localization accuracy, reducing localization error by more than 20%, and better computation efficiency, cutting time by more than 40%, compared with state-of-the-art approaches.
